newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on correction.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down on correction.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Wednesday on a technical correction, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 3,402 yuan ($410) per tonne, losing 25 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,395 yuan per tonne and a high of 3,416 yuan.
July fell 11 to 3,409, September was down 20 to 3,410 and November rose 19 to 3,420.
Combined volume rose to 7,200 tonnes from 2,800.
Soybeans opened lower on profit-taking and moved at low levels for most of the session, but traders said most investors were optimistic about the market's future movement.
"The day's fall was only a technical correction and I can't see it reversing the upward trend in the coming few days," one trader said.
Traders said improved fundamentals had finally begun to benefit long-position holders after a prolonged bearish performance.
